text:
Maria (PM): quick sync — a couple of prospects and one enterprise customer pushed hard for an embeddings API that supports: variable dims (768 / 1024 / 1536), large bulk ingestion, and a response shape that plugs directly into FAISS pipelines. need to lock MVP scope + launch criteria today. high level asks: sync small batches, async bulk ingest, and minimal friction for customers who already have 768-d indexes. any strong opinions?

Ravi (Eng-ML): we can support multiple dims but there are runtime costs. our serving runtime is optimized for a fixed vector width at model-load time (tensor layouts, kernel selection). supporting arbitrary dims means maintaining multiple model artifacts and more scheduling complexity. suggestion: ship MVP with two variants: 1536 (default, higher quality) and 768 (compat path). keep 1024 for later unless a customer signs up that needs it ASAP.

Mike (Eng-Platform): +1 to 2 variants. implementation notes: separate model instances per dim, different batching heuristics. sync endpoint can handle up to ~1024 inputs per request on our current infra if we cap total bytes; otherwise memory spikes. for async bulk ingest we should offer a job API that accepts NDJSON or compressed tar uploads. also need request-level guards: max_payload_bytes and max_inputs to avoid OOM.

Noah (Sales): customers I talked to: two mid-market SaaS teams use 768 and will push back if it's not available. enterprise is OK with 1536 if unit price is justified. 1024 isn't a hard ask today. having a clear migration story is important for renewals.

Susan (Customer Success): operational requirements from customers: nightly backfills of 100k-500k docs, incremental real-time inserts (~1000/day), and eventually snapshot re-indexing. they prefer async job APIs for backfills + webhooks on job completion. docs/examples showing how to ingest into FAISS or Pinecone are critical for success.

Ravi (Eng-ML): proposal for API MVP:
```
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "rw-embed-1536",   // default model id for high quality
  "input": ["...", "..."],
  "async": false
}
```
Sync limits: max_inputs = 1024, max_payload_bytes = 4_000_000 (4MB) per request.
Async bulk job:
```
POST /v1/embeddings/jobs
Content-Type: application/gzip
Body: NDJSON or tar.gz of documents
Response: { "job_id": "..." } -> webhook callback on completion
```
Return format (MVP): simple JSON list of float arrays per input (float32). example: 
{ "data": [ { "embedding": [0.123, -0.54, ...], "index": 0 }, ... ] }
Rationale: easy to plug into FAISS; easy for users to debug. Later we can add compressed/packed base64 or float16 to reduce bandwidth.

Mike (Eng-Platform): runtime constraints: float32 arrays are verbose (bandwidth cost). for now OK for MVP but we must measure tokenization + serialization overhead in our SDKs. batching rules: prefer dynamic batching with per-request size cap; also implement prefix caching for repeated inputs in production. we should add a per-customer rate limiter for async ingestion to protect shared infra.

Ravi (Eng-ML): model selection: start with two published model aliases: rw-embed-1536 and rw-embed-768. both have vetted perf/quality profiles. put 1536 as the default. quantized variants only behind Dedicated/reserved for cost-sensitive customers.

Susan (Customer Success): acceptance criteria from customers: 1) SDK example completes a 100k doc backfill in reasonable time (documented throughput) 2) clear mapping doc showing how to migrate from 768 -> 1536 3) webhooks and retry semantics documented 4) GA docs + sample FAISS ingestion notebook.

Noah (Sales): add pricing guidance in docs: per-vector pricing and bulk-job discounts for committed customers. that reduces objections.

Maria (PM): proposed launch criteria (MVP):
- Supported models: rw-embed-1536 (default), rw-embed-768 (compat)
- Sync endpoint: /v1/embeddings with max_inputs=1024, max_payload_bytes=4MB, return float32 arrays in JSON
- Async endpoint: /v1/embeddings/jobs with NDJSON/gzip support, job status + webhook callbacks
- Latency SLOs: single input p95 < 150ms; batch 16 p95 < 500ms; bulk job throughput documented in runbook
- Stability: pass 24h soak at expected traffic profile and a 500k-doc backfill test in staging
- Docs: SDK snippets, FAISS notebook, migration plan, pricing guidance
- Testing: end-to-end integration test with sample FAISS index + ingestion script

Ravi (Eng-ML): I can run model perf tests and provide p95 numbers by EOD. we'll also push a quantized (int8) path for Dedicated later.

Mike (Eng-Platform): I'll scope infra changes: two model artifacts, batching caps, async job infra, rate limits, and webhook retry pipeline. estimate: 3 sprint tasks + 1 infra spike for large file uploads.

ci-bot: deploy scheduled: embeddings/mvp-infra -> staging at 1789123480 :white_check_mark:

Susan (Customer Success): :thumbsup: will prep the FAISS notebook and sample customer playbook.

Maria (PM): decision summary for the board: MVP supports two dims (1536 default + 768 compat), sync + async ingestion, JSON float32 responses, explicit payload caps. next-phase: add 1024 model alias, compressed/packed embeddings, streaming/partial results, and direct DB connectors. if nobody objects, i'll mark this as the prioritized scope and start writing the PRD. please reply with objections by EOD.

Noah (Sales): 👍 prefer we fast-track the FAISS notebook in marketing collateral.

Ravi (Eng-ML): no objections. I'll post perf numbers and a short note on expected storage per vector (1536 dims ~ 6KB float32 -> ~6.1KB).

Mike (Eng-Platform): no objections from infra side, will add risk items to the ticket (large uploads, oom, rate-limiter tuning).

Maria (PM): thanks — I'll open the PRD and link this thread.
